findings.finding: Insights: From sum equations get b+Bs=10, a+As=20. So a=20‑As, b=10‑Bs. Use product equations: a·As=4b·Bs and a(As‑5)=b(Bs+5). Search integer As∈[5,19], Bs∈[0,9] → unique solution a=10, b=5. Product ages=50. Pitfall: ensure As≥5 (post‑transfer) and ages>0.

Insights: From Alice’s “sum double” and Bob’s “give‑5 makes sums equal”, get B+b=10, A+a=20. Then a=20−A, b=10−B. Use product equations: A(20−A)=4B(10−B) and A(15−A)=B(15−B). The latter gives A+B=15. Plug into first → A=10, B=5. Product A·B=50. Pitfall: mis‑interpreting “product” as (age+sweets) product; must be age·sweets.
